title: Why Triangle Inequality?
excerpt: Ever wondered why any axioms related to "distance between any two points" must satisfy the "Triangle Inequality"? Let's understand from scratch!
content:
# A Fun Analogy:
Suppose you're planning a road trip.
Kolkata to Delhi is approximately $\textbf{1470}$ km approx., Delhi to Chennai is $\textbf{2181}$ km approx., and Chennai to Kolkata is $\textbf{1700}$ km approx. 
Then Kolkata $\to$ Delhi $\to$ Chennai is approx. 3651 km, whereas Kolkata $\to$ Chennai is just 1700 km approx. Why? Obviously you know the reason. The key principle: <mark class="mark-blue">Any detour must be greater than our equal to the direct path</mark>
, also known as the "Triangle Inequality". But the notion of distance in this case though understandable and commonly used is very trivial, so why not bend the notion a little bit.
For example you've become a professor at some prestigious University like IISc Bangalore. Every student is brilliant in their own way, but then also you wants to  measure the relative brilliance of each student. You define a distance function which takes the score of any two students as parameter and give the relative output like this :
$$ d(\text{X}, \text{Y}) = |(Score_X) - (Score_Y) |^2$$
Let's assume, Ashish scored 80, Swapna scored 70 and Meghna scored 60. According to our definition of distance:
1) $d(\text{Ashish}, \text{Meghna}) = (80 - 60)^2$
2) $d(\text{Ashish}, \text{Swapna}) + d(\text{Swapna}, \text{Meghna}) = 100 + 100 = 200$


Does this forms a distance function? Does this satisfy the famous "Triangle Inequality"? 
According to the formula, Ashish and Meghna are further apart than the sum of the two intermediate gaps. The triangle inequality is violated. And the consequence is real if you tried to cluster students by "similarity" using this formula, students who are genuinely close in performance could end up in completely different groups.

title: Symmetry in Nature
excerpt: A case study on Symmetric Patterns evident in nature called "fractals", asking why they tends to occur, and is there any way to classify them(?).
content: # Symmetry: An Introduction What is Symmetry? The formal definition goes like this: "Symmetry is the characteristic of a body, to remain invariant under certain transformations or actions, being performed on it." Equationally it means if: $$ f:X \to R $$ is a function defined on the domain: $$ X \subset R \implies f(X) = X \quad \forall x\in X$$ All the points remain "invariant" under the restricted function "$ f|_{X}$ ". If the "body" is an abstract mathematical structure like a group, a graph or a vector space, the symmetries are the automorphisms. The term "automorphism" derives from the Greek prefix "auto-" meaning "self" and "morphe" meaning "form" or "structure", thus translating to "self-structure". It was first used in 1862 in the $\textit{ "Report of the British Association for the Advancement of Science"}$. Similarly I should give the origin and history of the word "Symmetry". Comes directly from the Latin word "symmetria" meaning relation of parts, proportion. In the 1590s the was attributed mostly in reference with proportion and commensurability of the human body. A new word that I recently learnt while researching is "$\textit{eurythmic}$" meaning "rhytmical, well-proportioned", just a fun word I wanted to share nothing else.😊 You can check the link for detailed information: https://www.etymonline.com/word/symmetry Symmetric patters and data in this universe is very relevant and in deeper sense it is what, helps us to study the laws of the nature. Let's enter the vast world of "Symmetry" and "Abstraction" using a simple example - The Rubik's Cube (source - https://web.osu.cz/~Zusmanovich/teach/books/visual-group-theory.pdf) # The Rubik's Cube Invented in the 1974 by Erno Rubik of Budapest, Hungary, this simple tool used for entertainment by us all, is in itself a whole mathematical world having its own sets of rules and regulations. The Human mind is very pattern oriented. It tries to grab any symmetrical data it can grab, and extrapolate it to come to a conclusion. The Symmetry in nature, that we can see around us are in some sense, the amalgamation of structured, pattern oriented data and geometry. Whenever we collect Raw data from scientific readings, most of it is "noise", the numbers that are inbuilt choatic, and can't be interpreted to produce any inference.
